newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Buba's Schieber sees no dlr impact from gold row.
newsitem.headline: Buba's Schieber sees no dlr impact from gold row.

text.p: Bundesbank council member Helmut Schieber said recent events in Germany had not affected the dollar, whose current strength was due to the strong U.S. economy.
Asked whether recent events in Germany had an unusual affect on the dollar, Schieber said:

"You can't say that the dollar exchange rate has developed in an extraordinary manner. We had fluctuations in the past without specific reasons," he told reporters at the Bank for International Settlements (BIS).

The Bundesbank has criticised a plan by the German government to revalue the German central bank's assets. A basic agreement was reached last week, which meant that Bonn would first receive any additional money from 1998.
"The main reason (for the dollar rate) is that America's economy has developed significantly better than the economy in Continental Europe," he added.
